construct: Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in LEMD3 and classically combines connective-tissue nevi with osteopoikilosis, a pattern of multiple small sclerotic bone foci.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Connective-tissue nevi plus symmetric periarticular osteopoikilosis and heterozygous LEMD3 loss identify Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Melorheostosis can also involve LEMD3-pathway abnormalities, but its radiographic pattern is asymmetric flowing cortical hyperostosis, not the symmetric osteopoikilosis plus connective-tissue nevi presented here. Camurati-Engelmann, osteopetrosis, and osteochondromas have different skeletal patterns.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The combined skin phenotype, osteopoikilosis pattern, family history, and germline LEMD3 loss make Buschke-Ollendorff uniquely best despite the biologic relationship between LEMD3 and melorheostosis.
